newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Colombia says ACPC coffee exports need revision.
newsitem.headline: Colombia says ACPC coffee exports need revision.

text.p: A coffee export program drawn up by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) needs to be revised for the first half of this year, particularly as far as robusta coffee exports are concerned, said Colombia's top coffee official.
"We agree that we have to make a revision of the program and organise the quantity of robusta coffee," Jorge Cardenas, head of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation, told Reuters.

ACPC members are to meet in Rio de Janeiro on January 23 to discuss a proposal by African nations to cut around 2.5 million 60-kg bags from exports between January to June 1997 due to declining prices.
The exact details of the proposal are only expected to be known on Thursday.
Colombia has already voiced its support for further reductions at a meeting with African officials in Bogota last month.
Cardenas did not rule out the possibility of some cuts in arabica exports, but pointed to a recent rise in arabica prices.
"(The cuts) could include some arabica, but the market has been changing a lot...We have to see with the rest of producers. It is too early to say at the moment," Cardenas said.
Under a plan agreed by ACPC members in May last year, member exports in January to June should not exceed 26.28 million bags.

Cardenas talked to Reuters in a telephone interview after his arrival in Rio de Janeiro for a three-day international coffee seminar which begins January 20 ahead of the ACPC meeting. Cardenas will speak on January 22 on price perspectives.
The ACPC's secretary-general, who also has arrived in Rio to speak at the coffee conference, was optimistic ACPC members would agree on measures to try and improve returns for robusta producers.

"We are going to evaluate the market. The situation for robustas is very difficult. Robusta prices are harming producers...I think there is a good possibility of reaching an agreement on how to address the situation," Roberio Oliveira da Silva told Reuters by telephone.
While looking ahead to the first half of 1997, member countries would not begin to think forward to 1997/98 (July/ June) at this meeting, da Silva said.
"This is an extraordinary meeting so the only thing on the agenda is the request made by the Africans," he said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
